previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was readmitted for acute decompensated heart failure due to medication non-adherence and increased fluid intake. He presented with chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and bilateral lower extremity edema after running out of torsemide and drinking excess water. Treatment included IV furosemide and careful diuresis, which improved his symptoms and reduced his weight from 139.5 kg to 129.2 kg. His kidney function declined during diuresis, with creatinine peaking at 3.0, leading to temporary holding of diuretics. Creatinine improved to 2.4 at discharge. A right heart catheterization confirmed elevated filling pressures. He was discharged home with instructions to hold torsemide for two days, monitor weight, and follow up for lab testing before restarting diuretics.

Brief Hospital Course:
Brief Hospital Course:
====================================================
___ M h/o CHF, CAD, DM, HTN, HLD presenting with increased 
dyspnea, orthopnea, 10 kg weight gain and peripheral edema in 
the setting of acute on chronic systolic heart failure due to 
two days of missed torsemide doses, admitted for IV diuretic 
therapy. 

Acute Issues:
=======================================================
#Acute on chronic systolic heart failure: 
Presented with symptoms of leg swelling and increased dyspnea on 
exertion. Initially he was started on IV lasix drip with good 
diuresis. While we hoped to diurese patient further, he did not 
want to stay for continued IV diuresis and wished to be 
discharged. Accordingly, decision was made to discharge patient 
on higher dose torsemide (160mg) with close outpatient follow up 
appointment w/ Dr. ___ on ___ to be examined and have 
CHEM10 checked. For afterload reduction, his dose of hydralazine 
was increased. He was also discharged on his previous doses of 
Imdur, Spironolactone, and digoxin. Weight on discharge was 132 
kg, down from 140 kg at admission.

#H/o CAD s/p stents: 
Ruled out for ACS while here. He is being continued on Aspirin 
81 mg, atorvastatin, and plavix.

#H/o VT: 
Occasional 5 beat runs of VT while here. Asymptomatic. Continued 
on home Amiodarone dose.

#CKD: 
The patient presented with a creatinine of 1.6 which increased 
to 2.3 by discharge. The increase while here was likely due to 
diuretic use, but his discharge creatinine was actually 
consistent with recent baseline prior to admission.  
  
# HTN: Hydralazine was increased from 20mg TID to 30mg TID for 
better BP control. He was continued on metoprolol succinate XL 
75 mg po qd. Patient was given compression stockings, extensive 
education regarding CHF management and importance of medication 
adherence. 

Transitional Issues:
==============================================
1. Patient has an extensive history of medication non-adherence 
and would benefit from continued re-inforcement of importance of 
such therapy
2. Patient was discharged w/ compression stockings to improve 
peripheral edema
3. Patient would benefit from consideration of outpatient ACE 
inhibitor therapy if he is found to be adherent to medication 
dosing. 
4. BNP on discharge was ___, weight was 132 kg
5. Pt should weigh himself daily, and call Dr. ___ 
should his weight increase or decrease by more than 3lbs as he 
may need an adjustment in his torsemide dose.
